transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught part of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, and it’s been causing problems.
Do you find your mind wandering when people are talking to you?

Yeah, that’s pretty much what happens. Someone will be talking right to me, like my supervisor or my wife, and I think I’m listening, but then a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of it. Then I have to ask them to say it again.
Do you find that your mind is wandering to other things when this happens, or are you just having trouble paying attention to what's being said?

Yeah, I think it’s more that I’m not really taking in what they’re saying. Like they’ll be talking right to me, and I realize a minute later I only caught half of it. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, and that’s what’s been getting me in trouble.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finish speaking?
Yes, I do. In meetings especially, I’ll answer before my supervisor even finishes the question. Sometimes I’m already talking, and then I realize I didn’t even let him get to the important part.
Do you have trouble organizing your daily tasks or keeping track of time?
I’m not really sure on that one. I mean, I get through my day somehow, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s organizing things or time that’s the problem.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking through the consequences?

Yeah, I do. At work I’ll jump in on somebody else’s setup without really stopping to think, like reaching in to fix it or telling them how to do it. I don’t wait for them to ask or for my turn, and then it turns into an argument because I’ve already stepped on their toes.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble sitting still?
Yes. If I have to sit still, it feels like this pressure building up in my chest and my legs. Like I need to move or do something right then, or I’m going to crawl out of my skin.
Were you often overly active or restless as a child?

Yeah, I was. Even when I was little, before middle school, teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn’t stay put. I’d call out answers, butt into other kids’ work, stuff like that. I got in trouble for it a lot.
Do you have trouble following through on instructions or finishing tasks at home, similar to what you described happening at work?
I’m not really sure. I mean, at home I get things done enough, I guess. I can’t think of a clear example like at work. What kind of instructions do you mean?
Do you often fidget or tap your hands or feet when you're sitting?

Yeah, all the time. If I’m sitting in a safety huddle or even at dinner, my leg’s usually bouncing. I’ll be messing with a pen or my keys, and people tell me I’m shaking the whole bench or table without even realizing it.
Have you had trouble paying attention or acting impulsively for as long as you can remember, even as a young child?

Yeah, pretty much as long as I can remember. Even before middle school, teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn’t sit still. I’d call out answers or get into other kids’ work, and I was in trouble for it a lot.
Do you also fidget or have trouble sitting still when you're at home or in other places outside of work?

Yeah, it’s not just at work. At home, if I’m sitting at the dinner table, my leg is usually going the whole time. I’ll be messing with my keys or a pen if there’s one there, and people will tell me I’m shaking the bench or the table and I don’t even notice I’m doing it.
Have these problems with attention and impulsivity caused you significant distress or gotten in the way of your relationships or work?

Yes, definitely. At work it’s gotten bad enough that I’ve had formal warnings, and I worry I could lose my job if I don’t get it under control. I also worry about making a mistake that could cause a safety problem on the line.

At home, it causes problems too. My wife and kids get frustrated because I’ll disrupt routines instead of helping things go smoothly. It’s stressful.
